references.text: Shares the motif of complete protection and safety in God's hand, where no enemy can snatch away the believer.
The direct prophetic background for Jesus' self-understanding as the good shepherd who gives his people eternal life and protects them from being snatched away.
Connects the shepherd motif with the promise of an everlasting covenant and a secure existence on God's holy mountain, parallel to the promise of eternal life.
Confirms that God's gift of eternal life is tied to knowing Him, and that this gift is secured by the Father so that no one can take it away.
Expresses the same theological principle: that none of those given to the Son will be lost, but will rise on the last day.
Confirms that believers have eternal life and know it, reflecting the claim that they have eternal life and will not perish.
